subject: AcmeHealth — GDPR / DPA / SCC selection (post-call recap & next steps)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 15:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery call — GDPR / SOC2 recap & next steps

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for taking the call earlier — great to meet you and Ben. Quick recap and proposed next steps on the GDPR / DPA / SCC items we discussed:

- Redwood SOC 2: In progress — SOC 2 Type II audit planned for Q2 2028; we have an interim controls summary available. Rishi will share a control coverage summary.
- DPA: We can provide our standard DPA. Attached is Redwood_DPA_v1.2.pdf for your legal team to review.
- SCCs: We typically recommend SCC Module 2 (Processor to Controller) for SaaS ingestion scenarios. I attached an SCC_module_matrix_v2.xlsx that maps module choices to common deployment patterns and obligations.
- Controller/Processor roles: From today's discussion my understanding is AcmeHealth is the Controller and Redwood acts as Processor for customer-provided data. Please confirm whether Acme expects Redwood to act as Controller for any derived/aggregated analytics (e.g., for benchmarking).

Proposed next steps:
1) Sophie / legal to confirm controller/processor alignment.
2) Redwood to provide DPA + SCC matrix (attached) — please flag any redlines.
3) Schedule a 30-min follow-up with Rishi (security) and Marissa (commercial) if helpful.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v1.2.pdf, SCC_module_matrix_v2.xlsx

Thanks,

Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0182

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acmehealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Clark <ben.clark@acmehealth.com>, Sophie Lim <sophie.lim@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 18:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery call — GDPR / SOC2 recap & next steps

Thanks Neha — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Controller/Processor: Correct that AcmeHealth is Controller for patient/customer data we upload. For aggregated/derived metrics that Acme licenses back to us (e.g., anonymized benchmarks), we generally expect Redwood to be Processor unless we explicitly contract otherwise. We'll confirm with legal.
- SOC 2: Good to know the audit is scheduled; can you send the interim control summary (Rishi)? That will help our audit team.
- Subprocessors: Please send the current subprocessors list and any planned additions.

Sophie — can you review the attached DPA once Neha shares it and indicate if Module 2 is acceptable or if we should request Module 1?

Appreciate it — can we aim to have initial legal feedback by end of next week?

Best,
Alex
Head of IT Compliance | AcmeHealth
alex.turner@acmehealth.com

From: Sophie Lim <sophie.lim@acmehealth.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acmehealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Clark <ben.clark@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery call — GDPR / SOC2 recap & next steps

Hi Neha / Alex,

Thanks — quick legal view and info request: we agree the default is Controller (Acme) / Processor (Redwood) for customer data. However, we need:

- A completed SCC matrix that maps which module you propose and why (we received Module 2 suggestion; please include rationale for any hybrid approach).
- Subprocessors list (current + planned) and a notice process for additions.
- Confirmation of data export controls and retention periods (we need to confirm retention is configurable per customer).
- For DPA: please include an editable doc (we prefer Track Changes) — we may have standard redlines around liability caps and audit rights.

If you can get the SCC matrix, DPA, and subprocessors list to us today/tomorrow, we'll review and aim to provide initial legal feedback by next Friday.

Thanks,
Sophie Lim
Senior Counsel — Privacy & Security | AcmeHealth
sophie.lim@acmehealth.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lim <sophie.lim@acmehealth.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery call — GDPR / SOC2 recap & next steps

Hi Sophie / Alex — thanks for the quick responses. Attached and linked:

- Redwood_DPA_v1.2.pdf (attached) — editable Word version available on Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/ACME-Redwood-Sec
- SCC_module_matrix_v2.xlsx (attached) — shows Module 2 recommendation and notes on hybrid scenarios for analytics.
- subprocessors_list.csv (attached) — current subprocessors and planned near-term additions. We will include a standard 30-day notice process for new subprocessors in the DPA.

Short answers to your bullets:
- Retention: Customer-configurable retention windows per route; default retention is 30 days for raw request data with options for longer retention under contract. We can document configurable settings in the DPA.
- Exports & audit: Customers can request data export; we offer logs for data access. We support SOC 2 auditor access under NDA.
- Editable DPA: I uploaded an editable copy to the Drive link above and sent a DocuSign preview (link included).

Next steps I propose: 1) Sophie to review DPA + SCC matrix; 2) schedule 30-min legal + security follow-up (Rishi) if there are substantive redlines; 3) Marissa to coordinate commercial terms if any obligations change.

I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for next week — suggested times are Tue/Wed 30-min slots.

Thanks,

Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0182
